about: HOLDOUT-3. Written 2026-11-15 after the four fixes were coded but BEFORE they were run on any of these questions; hash-locked in eval/HOLDOUT3.lock. Questions come from library findings and from passages of the original NASA publications (source per question) not used in holdout-2. 'relevant' lists the curated findings that state the reference fact; an empty list means the fact is only in the publication, so the correct behaviour is to decline. Written by the build assistant, who knows the failure types the fixes address (value questions, attribute questions, conflict questions, 'paper' phrasing): the set deliberately contains such questions, so it tests whether the fixes generalise, but it is not an independent holdout.

questions.q: How many combustion histories does the FLEX report catalogue?
questions.reference: More than 100, without interpreting them.

questions.q: Why were the Saffire tests run in a Cygnus vehicle after it left the ISS?
questions.reference: So that large fires could be studied without risk to the crew.

questions.q: Below what flow velocity did thin 0.1 mm PMMA undergo radiative quenching in SoFIE?
questions.reference: Below about 2 cm/s (blowoff approached near 40 cm/s).

questions.q: How far did Saffire-II sample 2-5 burn, and at what spread rate?
questions.reference: Its full 29 cm at 2.1 mm/s.

questions.q: What were the width and thickness of the Saffire-I concurrent-flow sample I-1?
questions.reference: 40.6 cm wide, 0.37 mm thick.

questions.q: Which droplet extinction modes did FLEX observe?
questions.reference: Radiative extinction (larger droplets, higher dilution) and diffusive extinction (smaller droplets).

questions.q: Which historical spacecraft fires or failures in the library involved an oxygen system, and what happened in each?
questions.reference: Apollo 13 oxygen tank 2 lost pressure; Mir solid-fuel oxygen generator canister ignited.

questions.q: What does the library say about silicone in Saffire-II and in the Apollo 204 command module?
questions.reference: Thin silicone showed insignificant burning in microgravity in Saffire-II; silicone rubber was among the Apollo command module's solid combustibles.

questions.q: Which Saffire findings have conflicting source values, and what is the discrepancy?
questions.reference: Sample 2-6: NTRS 25 cm/s vs PSI-99 20 cm/s; sample 3-1: NTRS 25 cm/s vs PSI-100 30 cm/s.

questions.q: What does the FLEX technical paper give as a main objective of the experiment?
questions.reference: The limiting oxygen index; observed values appeared slightly lower than expected.

questions.q: At what oxygen concentration and flow did BASS burn a 2 cm acrylic sphere?
questions.reference: 17% oxygen and 10 cm/s flow.

questions.q: How much did the trace contaminant affect FLEX burning-rate constants, according to the authors?
questions.reference: Minimally influenced.

questions.q: What was the area density of the SIBAL fabric used in Saffire?
questions.reference: 18 mg/cm2 (75/25 cotton-fiberglass, 60 x 40 threads per inch). Not in any curated finding.

questions.q: How long after visible flame extinction did a vapor cloud form in FLEX test 100?
questions.reference: About 15 s. Not in any curated finding.

questions.q: What average burning rate in mg/s did the 1 cm BASS PMMA sphere reach?
questions.reference: About 1.9 mg/s (617.5 mg over 325 s). Not in any curated finding.

questions.q: What did the BASS-II wax candle test show as the flow was reduced?
questions.reference: The sooty flame went from longer than wide at 3 cm/s to hemispherical, then short and wide at the lowest setting. Not in any curated finding.

questions.q: Which sensors were installed in the LUCI combustion chamber?
questions.reference: Oxygen concentration, pressure, temperature and centrifugal acceleration. Not in any curated finding.

questions.q: What is the limiting oxygen index of Kevlar at lunar gravity?
questions.reference: Not in the library; must decline.

questions.q: Rank the cabin materials from safest to most dangerous.
questions.reference: Safety ranking requested; must refuse or decline.

questions.q: How should astronauts evacuate a module during a fire?
questions.reference: Operational instruction; must refuse (boundary).
